[5] search_document: cozy builder, Jean Pierre, asked me if I knew the difference between the strong pitch system and the Electric Pitch Trim SystemEEle sold on Long EZ.com. The "Strong" pitch trim system is a small electric motor from an electric screwdriver with a custom compression spring cartridge. I've had one for 10 years. After a few small issues, it basically works fine. There's a little hysteresis, and it's too sensitive at high speeds, but all electric pitch trims have the sensitivity issue on canards unless they have a good pulse width modulator hooked up to an airspeed switch. The trim system shown on is a "Davenport" cantilever spring driven by the same actuator used for the landing brake. Search on "davenport" trim systems which can be manual or electric . It's a modification smaller of the trim system used on the Velocity, I believe. You can make one for yourself for about $3 worth of composites and the electric actuator I made one, but then didn't have the space behind the panel to retrofit it, so sold the actuator and kept the "Strong" system. These systems don't have hysteresis and are far simpler although larger than the "Strong" system. If I were starting from scratch, I'd use the "Davenport" system, but I'd make it myself. But as I say, the "Strong" system has worked for me for 10 years and shows no signs of giving up the ghost. My $0.02. Marc J. Zeitlin mailto marc z... alum.mit.edu Copyright c 2012 !

There isn’t survey data here to say definitively which is most common. **The plans trim is probably the most commonly installed**, since it’s the standard plans option and some builders choose it because it’s straightforward and quick to build. [2]

**Davenport seems to be the most often recommended by people expressing a preference.** Some flyers say they love it, and one experienced builder said he’d choose it if starting from scratch; it’s also described as simple and without the Strong system’s hysteresis. [3][5] It does need careful tuning for the individual aircraft, and its spring needs inspection and proper design. [4][13]

**Strong trim has satisfied some owners**, including one who used it for years, but reports also mention sensitivity, hysteresis, and repair or parts concerns. [5][7][15]

So, as a rough summary: **plans may be most common; Davenport may be the preference among the flyers quoted here.** That’s anecdotal, not a reliable count. Whichever system you choose, make sure it can be overridden safely in a trim runaway and checked through full control travel. [1][10]
